linux.intro: Install v4l2loopback and load it with administrator rights. The studio does not install it for you.
linux.install:
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install v4l2loopback-dkms
# Fedora (RPM Fusion)
sudo dnf install v4l2loopback
# Arch Linux
sudo pacman -S v4l2loopback-dkms
linux.load: sudo modprobe v4l2loopback devices=1 video_nr=10 card_label="ugoe studio" exclusive_caps=1
linux.after: Then turn the virtual camera on again. To load it at every boot, put “v4l2loopback” in /etc/modules-load.d/ and the options above in /etc/modprobe.d/.

videoGroup.intro: Add yourself to the “video” group, which can open the video devices.
videoGroup.after: Then log out and back in (or restart the computer) and turn the virtual camera on again.

guide.windows: On Windows 10, capture the output window in OBS Studio and use OBS's “Start Virtual Camera” instead.
guide.reinstall: Run the studio installer again. Registering the camera needs administrator rights.

api.heading: Studio API
api.enable: Let other apps on this computer control the studio
api.hint: Tools such as Stream Deck or chat bots can switch scenes, expressions and motions. Only apps on this computer can connect, and you approve each new app here.
api.error: The studio API is not available: {{message}}
api.tokenHint: Enter the address and the token in the app you connect. The token is needed only for the first connection; keep it to yourself.
api.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
api.regenerateBody: Apps that have not been approved yet can no longer connect with the old token. Approved apps keep working.
api.revokeBody: The app is disconnected and has to ask for approval again with the token.
api.approveTitle: {{name}} wants to connect to the studio
api.approveBody: Approve only apps you started yourself. Read only lets the app see scenes and expressions; read and control also lets it switch them and move parameters.

source.heading: Browser source (OBS)
source.enable: Serve a page for the OBS browser source
source.hint: Paste the URL into an OBS browser source to bring in the avatar with a transparent background. Only apps on this computer can open the page, and the page can only watch, not control.
source.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
source.urlHint: The URL contains a token that cannot be guessed. Do not show it to anyone or on stream.
source.port: Port {{port}} is shared with the control API. Change it in the Control API panel (the URL changes too).
source.regenerateBody: Browser sources with the old URL stop showing the avatar. Paste the new URL into OBS.
source.step1: In OBS, click + under Sources and choose Browser to add a new source.
source.step2: Paste the copied URL into URL.
source.step3: Set Width to {{width}} and Height to {{height}} (the output window size). The model keeps the scene placement as fractions of the size, so other sizes keep the same framing.
source.step3Free: Set Width and Height to match your stream (for example 1920 and 1080). The model keeps the scene placement as fractions of the size.
source.step4: The background is transparent. You can leave Custom CSS as the OBS default. If the scene has a color or image background, it is shown as well.
source.step5: Leave "Shutdown source when not visible" and "Refresh browser when scene becomes active" off, so swaying parts keep moving smoothly.
